context.title: A Statue and a Stone
context.summary: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell him both his dream and its meaning; Daniel, after praying with his friends, reveals a great statue of four metals shattered by a stone that becomes a mountain.
context.background: At verse 4 the text switches from Hebrew to Aramaic (the KJV's 'Syriack'), which continues to the end of chapter 7. The statue shows four kingdoms, beginning with Babylon as the head of gold. Traditionally the others are identified as Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome; many modern scholars see Media, Persia and Greece. Either way, God's kingdom replaces them all.

customs.note: Here a class of Babylonian scholars skilled in astrology and omens, not just the ethnic group. Interpreting dreams was a serious profession.

watchFor: Daniel's prayer of praise before he goes to the king (vv. 20–23).
'There is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets' (v. 28).

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Daniel
people.summary: Beltis protect the king!, the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).

people.name: Meshach
people.summary: One of the three Hebrew youths who were trained with Daniel in Babylon (Dan. 1:11, 19), and promoted to the rank of Magi. He and his companions were afterwards cast into the burning fiery furnace for refusing to worship the idol the king had set up, from which they were miraculously delivered (3:13-30).

people.name: Shadrach
people.summary: Aku’s command, the Chaldean name given to Hananiah, one of the Hebrew youths whom Nebuchadnezzar carried captive to Babylon (Dan. 1:6, 7; 3:12-30).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

events.title: Prophecies of Daniel
events.summary: Passage: Daniel 1:1–12:13. People: Daniel. Lasted about 72 years.
